sources.title: Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama
sources.evidence: July 18, 2023 announcement makes Llama 2 weights and code available, including pretrained and conversational fine-tuned versions.

sources.title: Llama-2-13b-chat-hf model card
sources.evidence: Identifies this repository as the 13B dialogue fine-tune converted to Transformers. Names Meta, text input/output, SFT/RLHF, and 4k context. Its 13B row explicitly excludes GQA. License acceptance is required for downloading weights. Reopened October 27: the exact repository still identifies the 13B dialogue fine-tune, with pretrained and fine-tuned variations and SFT/RLHF training.

sources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
sources.evidence: Table 1 lists the Llama 2 13B model with 4k context and no GQA. Sections 2.2 and 3 describe Transformer architecture and Chat fine-tuning. Appendix A.2.1 explicitly gives 4096 tokens. Section 5.1 reports emergent tool use without tool-use training. Reopened October 27: Section 1 explicitly calls Llama 2-Chat a fine-tuned Llama 2 version and releases 13B variants of each; Figure 4 shows base pretraining followed by SFT and RLHF. Section 3.2.3 describes smaller models learning from 70B rejection-sampled responses, a training-data distillation step rather than structural compression of the 13B base. No pruning, expert expansion, added modality or Chat vocabulary change is described.

sources.title: Llama 2 reference model implementation
sources.evidence: Original llama_v2 reference code implements causal attention, dense SwiGLU feed-forward layers, RMSNorm and RoPE; each Transformer block executes sequentially, without expert routing. Read from the branch resolved to this commit. Reopened October 27: the shared Transformer implementation contains dense attention and SwiGLU blocks, with no expert routing or Chat-specific structural branch.

sources.title: Llama 2 reference chat generation
sources.evidence: Chat messages have system, user and assistant roles and string content. The reference chat_completion interface generates assistant text; it does not declare a reasoning mode or structured native function-call interface. Reopened October 27: Llama.build constructs the shared Transformer from checkpoint parameters and sets its vocabulary size from the supplied tokenizer; text and chat completion use the same model generation path.

sources.title: Llama 2 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Names the custom Llama 2 Community License and July 18, 2023 release date. Grants limited use and redistribution rights subject to conditions, acceptable-use restrictions and additional commercial terms.

sources.title: Llama 2 reference repository README
sources.evidence: Separates pretrained models from fine-tuned dialogue models, documents release of model weights and a maximum supported sequence length of 4096 tokens. Llama 1 is assigned a separate branch. Reopened October 27: both pretrained and Chat examples use the same tokenizer.model path.

sources.title: Original Llama-2-13b-chat-hf configuration (gated)
sources.evidence: Direct public config retrieval again returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized on October 27, 2026. No gated configuration or weight tensors were accessed; no exact learned-parameter count is claimed.

sources.title: Later Llama model SKU utility
sources.evidence: The later llama2_13b_chat entry lists n_heads=40 and n_kv_heads=8, conflicting with the original 13B model card and paper, which explicitly exclude GQA. This later utility is not used to infer the released checkpoint topology or exact count.

sources.title: Mixtral of Experts — Table 2 active-parameter comparison
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 2 explicitly reports LLaMA 2 13B at 13B in the Active Params column. This is Mistral’s nominal inference-comparison convention for the base model, not a direct Meta active-count disclosure or an explicit 13B Chat row. Section 3 discusses active count in relation to inference compute. Table 3 has no active-count column and compares 70B, not 13B Chat; it is not used to establish this count.

sources.title: Original Llama 2 download manifest and shared tokenizer
sources.evidence: Read as source on October 27, 2026; script was not executed. The release script lists both 13B and 13B-chat and retrieves one shared tokenizer.model before selecting any model. Together with the common loader and Meta’s explicit fine-tuning lineage, this supports unchanged vocabulary and a nominal base-to-Chat count inference. No weights were downloaded.

name.note: Readable catalog name for the original 13B Chat checkpoint; the HF suffix denotes its serialization format.

developer.note: Meta is the original developer and publisher.

family.note: Llama 2 Chat belongs to the second-generation Llama family; distinguish its dialogue fine-tune from the base model and Llama 1.

release_date.note: The dated launch explicitly includes conversational fine-tunes; the license independently records the same version release date.

open_weights.note: Meta released downloadable pretrained and Chat weights, subject to license acceptance and access approval.

license.note: Custom community/commercial license with conditions; it is not Apache-2.0 or an unrestricted permissive license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh check retains Meta’s explicit nominal 13B size for this exact Chat checkpoint. The model card and paper both publish 13B Chat; this is a nominal developer specification, not a tensor-derived exact count.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal lineage inference: Mistral’s Mixtral Table 2 explicitly assigns the Llama 2 13B base model 13B Active Params. Meta identifies 13B Chat as the corresponding SFT/RLHF fine-tune; the shared dense implementation and tokenizer support retaining that nominal convention. The paper’s distillation uses 70B-generated training responses to fine-tune the existing smaller models and does not describe pruning or structural compression. No expert expansion, vocabulary change or new modality is documented. This is attributed to Mistral’s base-model comparison plus Meta’s Chat lineage, not a direct Meta disclosure of Chat active parameters or an exact per-token tensor census.

architecture.note: Dense causal Transformer with SwiGLU, RMSNorm and RoPE. Original release sources place 13B in the MHA variants and reserve GQA for larger models. The conflicting later SKU utility is not treated as checkpoint evidence.

context_window.note: Original training and documented inference context is 4096 tokens. This excludes later extensions and shorter demonstration cache settings.

modalities.note: The original model card explicitly specifies text-only input and output.

reasoning.note: No dedicated reasoning mode or separate reasoning output is specified for this checkpoint. Ordinary reasoning benchmarks and generated explanations do not establish that feature.

tool_call.note: The paper describes emergent prompted tool use, but its examples do not establish a native tool-call feature for exactly 13B Chat. The released interface is text chat; downstream wrappers are separate.

description.value: Meta's nominal 13B-parameter Llama 2 dialogue model, fine-tuned with supervised learning and RLHF, with text input/output and a 4,096-token context.
description.note: Makes the exact Chat variant and documented capabilities explicit without unsupported performance or tool-use claims.

patch.description: Meta's nominal 13B-parameter Llama 2 dialogue model, fine-tuned with supervised learning and RLHF, with text input/output and a 4,096-token context.
patch.notes: Total 13B is Meta’s nominal Chat specification. Active 13B is a nominal inference from Mistral’s published Llama 2 13B base comparison and Meta’s documented Chat fine-tuning lineage with shared dense architecture and tokenizer. Neither is an exact tensor count. The original 13B release uses MHA despite a conflicting later Meta SKU utility. Dedicated reasoning/tool-call features are not separately disclosed.

sources.label: Later Meta SKU utility (conflicts with original 13B attention specification)
Mistral Mixtral paper: nominal active-count comparison for Llama 2 13B base
Meta Llama 2 release manifest: shared tokenizer for base and Chat

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit preserves Meta’s nominal 13B total and resolves active parameters to a nominal 13B lineage inference. Mistral’s original Mixtral Table 2 explicitly lists 13B Active Params for Llama 2 13B base; Meta’s explicit 13B base-to-Chat SFT/RLHF lineage, shared dense implementation and shared tokenizer support carrying that convention to Chat. The paper’s response-data distillation does not describe structural compression. Table 3 supplies no 13B Chat active-count evidence, and the fresh search found no direct Meta active-count disclosure. The public configuration remains gated (401); exact tensor participation is not claimed and no weights were downloaded. The other twelve field assessments remain unchanged.
